Hi Angela / Tim —

Thanks again for the conversation last week. Attached is a short note + timeline with three pragmatic ways to structure Dedicated capacity for MedSprint. High-level summary below; full details and an onboarding timeline are in the attached files (medsprint_draft_mop.pdf, onboarding_timeline.xlsx).

Option A — Pilot-first (lowest up-front commit)
- Baseline: 8 x A100-equivalent GPUs (pilot cluster)
- Burst: up to 32 GPUs via pre-warmed burst lane for 2 months
- Ramp: convert pilot to reserved or scale to lane B at month 3 based on usage
- Tradeoffs: fastest time-to-live, higher unit cost while pilot active

Option B — Staged baseline (recommended for predictable SLA)
- Baseline: 40 x A100-equivalent GPUs (minimum reserved)
- Burst: additional 40 GPUs for short bursts (80 total)
- Ramp: linear increase to 80 baseline over 3 months (20 GPUs/month)
- Tradeoffs: lower unit cost, strong latency predictability, fits med-surge patterns you described

Option C — Conservative floor + aggressive burst (cost-sensitive)
- Baseline: 20 x GPUs
- Burst: 100 GPUs available via regional bursting and autoscale for traffic spikes
- Ramp: stepwise increases tied to MRR milestones (6-week cadence)
- Tradeoffs: lower committed footprint but requires more burst orchestration and monitoring

Key notes and constraints
- We can support KMS-backed keys and dedicated networking for Private deployments; see page 3 of the MOP for the KMS integration checklist.
- Pricing anchors in the attached PDF are estimates pending final exchange rate & term length.
- Lead time: standard activation for a 40-GPU lane is ~3–4 weeks for Dedicated; pilot lanes can be available in 5 business days with pre-approved configuration.

Ask: which option would you like pricing and a formal SOW for? If you want, we can scope a 6-week pilot (Option A) and a pathway to convert to Option B if performance/throughput targets are met.

Thanks —

Lauren Bishop

Hi Angela — great questions, answers and tweaks below; I also updated onboarding_timeline.xlsx with two ramp cadence options (attached).

1) Option B ramp speed: yes — we can support a compressed ramp (20 → 40 GPUs in 6 weeks) as a custom onboarding plan. The tradeoff is slightly higher near-term provisioning overhead; lead time remains ~3 weeks for baseline activation but we can pre-provision burst capacity earlier to cover spikes.

2) Pilot conversion credit: if you run Option A pilot and convert to reserved with us within 90 days, we will apply pilot usage as a one-time credit toward the first 3 months of reserved fees (details and thresholds in the attached MOP). I'll capture exact numbers in the SOW once you confirm target baseline.

3) KMS / encryption: KMS itself does not require a dedicated GPU node, but integrating customer-managed keys does require some additional setup in the Private control plane and a short security review (2–3 business days). It does not change the GPU count but does add ~5 business days to the activation timeline if you want customer KMS enabled at day zero.

4) Regional burst limits: burst lanes are region-scoped; we can provision regionally redundant burst pools (we recommend a primary + hot-standby region for your failover plan). I noted a multi-region burst addendum in the timeline worksheet.

Cancellation / decommissioning summary for procurement (short blurb you can share):
- Minimum notice for decommissioning reserved baseline: 30 days prior to the next billing cycle.
- Early termination: negotiated in SOW (standard options include pro-rated refunds for unused committed capacity after 60 days post-notice for annual contracts).

Recommended path (my suggestion): start with a 6-week compressed ramp to 40-GPU baseline (custom Option B). It balances predictability and your need for quicker capacity growth. If you prefer, we can start a 4-week pilot concurrently to validate traffic patterns before hitting committed baseline.

If that's acceptable, I'll have a pricing addendum and draft SOW ready by Thursday and loop in Finance & Solutions.

Best,

Lauren
